sentences.text:
Opposite Party
 ---
Coram :Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice Anubha Rawat Choudhary

---
 For the Petitioner : Ms. Alka Kumari, Advocate
 : Mr. Saurabh Tantia, Advocate

For the Opp. Party : Mr. D.C. Mishra, Advocate
 ---

09/16.05.2024 Heard the learned counsel of the parties.
2.

This petition has been filed challenging the Order dated 19.02.2019, passed by learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Dumka, in Original Maintenance Case No. 52 of 2017, whereby the maintenance case filed by the petitioner has been dismissed on the ground that the opposite party has been able to prove one of the exceptions under Section 125 (4) of Cr.P.C, wherein it has been mentioned that if the wife is living in adultery, she would not be entitled to receive maintenance or expenses of proceedings.
3.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the said finding has been recorded primarily by taking into consideration the content of the document whereby the PW2 and PW3, the parents of the petitioner had admitted their signature on Exhibit A and agreement executed between the parents of the parties on 01.09.2016, which showed that the petitioner had opted to leave her husband on her own on 31.08.2016 while leaving with her paramour.
The learned counsel submits that agreement between the parents could not be taken into consideration to come to a finding of adultery.

Mrs. Monika Rajak vs Kripasindhu Rajak on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98144975/
1 4.

The learned counsel for the opposite party has opposed the prayer and has submitted that during the pendency of this case, the case filed under section 498A of Indian Penal Code by the petitioner has ended in a compromise.
He has further submitted that so far as the impugned order is concerned, that is not the only document which has been taken into consideration but other attending facts have also been considered.

He has also submitted that the proceeding under Section 125 is essentially a summary proceeding and the findings recorded therein are only prima facie finding based on material on record and to arrive at such prima-facie finding of adultery, there were enough materials.

He has also submitted that the learned court has also recorded that the petitioner has left the company of the opposite party no. 2 without any reasonable excuse and therefore, the impugned order refusing to grant maintenance to the petitioner does not call for any interference.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has not disputed that the parties have settled their case under section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and have agreed to live separately.
A copy of the judgment passed under section 498A has been placed before this court.

6. After hearing the learned counsels for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court finds that the marriage between the parties is not in dispute which had taken place sometime in the month of November, 2010 and a child was also born out of wed-lock.
The petitioner had been living separately since 31.08.2016.
It further appears from the records that the petitioner had also filed a Matrimonial Suit No.49 of 2016 but the same was dismissed for default on 06.09.2016.
The learned court considered the materials and recorded a finding at paragraph no.19 that the opposite party was able to prove that the petitioner left her matrimonial home on her own on 31.08.2016.

The learned court has also considered the legal value of the documents wherein the parents of both the parties had come to an agreement that the relationship between the parties as husband and wife would seize and they cannot be compelled to live together as couple, was debatable as no such agreement could be binding between the parties (husband and wife).

However,
further material has been considered by the learned court to come to a finding that the respondent was able to prove that the petitioner left her matrimonial home on her own on 31.01.2016 and her allegation to the contrary could not be relied upon.

This Court finds that the learned court further recorded in para no.25 that the opposite party was able to prove one of the exceptions in section 125 (4) of Cr.P.C wherein it has been mentioned that if the wife is living in adultery, she would not be entitled to receive maintenance or expenses.

Further the learned court recorded that the totality of the circumstances and evidences discussed suggests that the petitioner had left her matrimonial home out of her own to live in the company of someone else.

7. This Court finds that the learned court has recorded a finding that the respondent was able to prove that the petitioner had left her matrimonial home on her own on 31.08.2016 and apart from that also recorded that the respondent was able to prove that the petitioner was living in adultery.
It is not in dispute that the proceeding under section 125 Cr.P.C is essentially a summary proceeding and the finding recorded therein are only prima facie finding and not conclusive in nature.
The finding that the petitioner had left the matrimonial house on her own on 31.08.2016 was itself enough to refuse maintenance to the petitioner.

This Court finds that the learned court has not recorded its findings solely on the agreement entered into between the parents of the parties, but has taken the entire facts and circumstances of the case to come to the findings.

Mrs. Monika Rajak vs Kripasindhu Rajak on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98144975/
2 8.
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court finds no reason to interfere with the impugned order refusing maintenance to the petitioner in revisional jurisdiction.
9. Accordingly, this revision is hereby dismissed.

(Anubha Rawat Choudhary, J.) Saurav Mrs. Monika Rajak vs Kripasindhu Rajak on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98144975/
